memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The same law applies to both the sin offering and the guilt offering: They belong to the priest who makes atonement with them. The priest who offers a burnt offering for anyone may keep its hide for himself.'" - Lev 7:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God provides for His servants through the very act of their service. The priest who made atonement received the offering. The priest who handled a burnt offering kept the hide — a genuinely valuable item, since leather was worth good money.

God had already said the Levites would receive no land. So He built their livelihood into the work itself.

This is characteristic of how God provides. He rarely drops provision out of the sky. He usually weaves it into obedience, into work, into ordinary faithfulness. The widow of Zarephath was fed as she kept making bread (1 Kgs 17:15-16). The disciples' nets filled when they let them down again (Lk 5:5-6).

Paul cited this exact principle: Don't you know that those who serve in the temple get their food from the temple...? In the same way, the Lord has commanded that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel (1 Cor 9:13-14).

There is a caution here too, which the sons of Eli would later ignore catastrophically (1 Sam 2:12-17). What God provides through ministry can be abused by those who begin to serve for what they can extract.

God's provision is real. It is also a trust.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I look for God's provision only in the extraordinary, missing it in the ordinary?
2. If I serve God in any capacity, are my motives clean about what I receive?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for providing through the ordinary work You give me. Keep my heart clean in whatever I receive from Your hand. Amen.
